text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- Bavarian week, a great success of Croatian diplomacy and economy, says Cratian general consul in Munich, Ivan Simek.
- Croatian stock market: Stocks reach record prices.

- Agriculture and food industry: Compared to the first seven months of 1995, the same period in 1996 has seen import of food and agricultural goods down from $585 million to$552, and export up from $316 million to $358.
- A record 2,961 exhibitors have taken part in the Zagreb Autumn Trade Fair.
- The members of the Zagreb city and county assembly to freeze their mandates so as to no longer take part in the Zagreb crisis.
- The Dayton Bosnia is not plausable, says Dr. Herwig Roggeman, international law expert and director of the Berlin Osteuropa Institute.
- Two hundred Croats apply daily for a Yugoslav visa, claims the Charge d'Affaires of the Yugoslav embassy in Zagreb, Veljko Knezevic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
